html:
SMTO-HTTP-0049 — SMTO's web request was stopped

GUID: 7965436e-a0d8-44cb-8ab2-5cc3014ca7bf
Slug: http-cancelled
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The request was stopped, either because someone selected Stop or because the same request was already running or had just been stopped. It may already have reached the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: look on the service for the change the task was making. Stopping cuts the connection but can't undo anything the service had already done.
  2. If this Run is still shown as running or stopping, wait until it has fully stopped before you start the task again. SMTO refuses a second copy of the same request while the first is still running or was stopped in the last few minutes.
  3. Only if the change didn't happen, start the task again as a new Run. Repeating a change that already went through could make it happen twice.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the change happened exactly once, or a new run completes it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting what you saw on the service. Don't repeat the change while you're unsure whether the first attempt went through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected or interrupted the HTTP execution: its execution ID was already active or cancelled within the last five minutes, or owned socket I/O raised IOCancelled after dispatch (effect unknown).

What this means

  • The execution identity was already active/recently cancelled, or socket ownership raised IOCancelled after execution began. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The execution identity was already active/recently cancelled, or socket ownership raised IOCancelled after execution began.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect executed/effect_unknown and the original identity; a rejected duplicate is not evidence that the original request did nothing.

How to fix it

  • Use the result's executed and effect_unknown flags and the Gateway log to tell whether cancellation happened before dispatch or mid-flight; inspect the target's state before re-issuing a write, and start a new run rather than reusing a cancelled execution.
  • Inspect cancellation provenance and remote state before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original owner settles and current remote state resolves any possible mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
